title: Lynx Insurance edge QA: multi-profile latency and unit-cost runbook
content:
Purpose:
Runbook and raw notes from the Lynx Insurance edge QA POC (May 2029). We measured latency distributions, steady-state throughput, cold-start behavior, and per-token unit cost across three deployment profiles: Hosted-Standard, Dedicated-A10X (8x GPU pool), and Private-VPC quantized (int8). Goal was to validate that Redwood Dedicated meets Lynx's p95 SLA (<= 450 ms for short prompts) and to provide concrete config recommendations for their production rollout.

Test matrix (short):
- Model: open-llama-13b-v2 (base fp16), and quantized-int8 variant from model catalog.
- Prompt palettes: small-query (12 tokens), mid-query (64 tokens), long-query (512 tokens).
- Traffic shapes: steady (200 qps), spike (burst to 2k qps sustained 30s), intermittent (poisson mean 100 qps).
- Warm/cold: warm KV cache vs cold-start per-node.
- Routing: prefer Dedicated pool; fallback to Hosted when Dedicated pool saturated.

Environment details:
- Hosted-Standard: mixed vCPU-backed nodes, multi-tenant, autoscaled (region us-west2).
- Dedicated-A10X: 8x A10X GPUs, continuous batching enabled, prefix caching ON, batch size cap 64.
- Private-VPC (customer infra): 4x A10X, model quantized-int8, compilation with kernel set B, no cross-node KV share.

Key numbers (aggregated; median of 3 runs):
1) Short prompts (12 tokens) - warm cache
- Hosted-Standard: p50 60 ms, p95 320 ms, max 780 ms, steady throughput 450 qps, cost estimate $0.016 per 1k tokens
- Dedicated-A10X: p50 32 ms, p95 110 ms, max 210 ms, steady throughput 1250 qps, cost estimate $0.005 per 1k tokens
- Private-VPC (int8): p50 40 ms, p95 130 ms, max 260 ms, steady throughput 980 qps, cost estimate $0.0038 per 1k tokens (note: infra amortized separately)

2) Mid prompts (64 tokens) - warm cache
- Hosted-Standard: p50 140 ms, p95 620 ms, steady throughput 220 qps, cost $0.032 per 1k tokens
- Dedicated-A10X: p50 78 ms, p95 220 ms, steady throughput 560 qps, cost $0.009 per 1k tokens
- Private-VPC (int8): p50 95 ms, p95 280 ms, steady throughput 420 qps, cost $0.0065 per 1k tokens

3) Long prompts (512 tokens) - warm cache
- Hosted-Standard: p50 780 ms, p95 2.4 s, throughput 28 qps, cost $0.28 per 1k tokens
- Dedicated-A10X: p50 410 ms, p95 980 ms, throughput 86 qps, cost $0.07 per 1k tokens
- Private-VPC (int8): p50 490 ms, p95 1.1 s, throughput 68 qps, cost $0.054 per 1k tokens

Burst behavior notes (spike to 2k qps):
- Dedicated pool with burst capacity enabled handled 2k qps for 22s before queueing rose; tail latencies spiked (p99 > 3s) during sustained bursts >20s. Autoscaling policy must be tuned: increase reactive scale-up aggression and pre-warm thresholds for predicted campaign windows.
- Hosted fallback activated at ~85% Dedicated utilization; observed ~15% increased p95 on routed requests due to model variance across instances.
- Private-VPC without cross-node KV sharing showed cold-start penalty ~+200 ms on the first few requests after node rotation; recommend enabling per-node warmers or shared cache layer if workload requires microsecond-level consistency.

Anomalies / Risks observed:
- We observed occasional 400 ms spikes on Dedicated-A10X tied to GC pauses (python runtime) in the custom preprocessor. Root cause: preprocessor thread pool config defaulting to 2 threads under load. Fix: raise to 8 and pin CPU affinity.
- Quantized-int8 variant produced 0.6% semantic drift on a small eval set (N=250 dialogs). For Lynx this is acceptable for classification/QL use-cases but not for legal-text summarization; recommend running model-evals on customer prompts for acceptance.
- Network egress cost on Private-VPC during large batch transfers can dominate if model artifacts are shuttled frequently. Suggest artifact caching strategy and local registry mirror.

Recommendations (quick):
1) Production config for policy: Dedicated-A10X pool with autoscale: target utilization 65%, scale step +2 nodes, cooldown 45s, burst capacity enabled (+25% for 60s). Pre-warm hooks triggered by feature-flagged campaign to avoid cold-starts.
2) Use quantized-int8 in Private only after acceptance eval; run a 1k prompt QA sweep comparing rouge/EM metrics.
3) Tune preprocessor thread pool, add CPU pinning, and instrument GC metrics in tracing dashboard.
4) Implement graceful fallback routing with jittered reroute and per-route latency budgets to avoid global p95 regressions when falling back to Hosted.
5) Add unit-cost monitoring to console: per-route tokens, per-model kernel selection, and per-region cost breakouts.

Action items (owners):
- Marco Li: run extended 24h soak with synthetic mixed-profile (deadline 2029-05-28) [JIRA-LYNX-2142].
- Evan Brooks: apply preprocessor thread pool fix + new image (PR-87), validate on staging (2029-05-18) - DONE.
- Sofia Grant: run acceptance eval on 1k real customer prompts for quantized model; produce pass/fail matrix (2029-05-24).
- Priya Nambiar: update proposal doc for Dedicated capacity commit sizing and cost delta (due 2029-05-30).

Appendix - quick checklist for field teams:
- Verify KV-prefix caching enabled for small-query dominant routes.
- Confirm batch size cap set to 64; if latency-sensitive, drop to 32 and monitor p50 change.
- For private infra: ensure model registry mirror exists and that kernel selection B is installed on all nodes.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Explore continuous-batching variant that isolates short prompts into smaller fast-path pools. Could reduce p95 20–30% for small-query dominated workloads.
- Consider per-customer model profiles exposed in Console (cost slider + latency SLO preview).

End of runbook.
